subject: RE: Sustained tail latency and error spike — BlueLeaf production impact
messages:
From: Tom Alvarez <tom@blueleafanalytics.com>
To: kimberly.park@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 1 Dec 2027 09:22:00 -0800
Subject: Urgent: Growing latency tail, errors & throughput drop — need help

Kimberly —

We're seeing a sustained degradation in production that started this morning (around 08:30 PST) and has been getting worse. Key symptoms:
- 99.9th percentile response time has climbed from ~2.1s to >12s for our LongForm endpoint.
- Intermittent 502/504s and internal server 5xx spikes (~2.2% error rate vs baseline 0.1%).
- Apparent throughput collapse: we get substantial queueing and backpressure; requests are being dropped once concurrency caps are hit.

This is impacting search indexing and nightly scoring jobs — conversions down, alerts firing. We've attached logs and a short packet capture from this morning: blueleaf-sla-incident-logs.zip.

We need an immediate mitigation plan and an ETA on root cause. If this requires exec attention / credits / capacity changes, flag them — we'll need answers for our leadership.

Tom
CTO, BlueLeaf Analytics
--
Attached: blueleaf-sla-incident-logs.zip (archive, 9.2MB)

1) Stand-up call: 10:00 PST with ops + engineering (joining link: https://zoom.us/j/123456789).
2) Evidence collection: Marissa, please pull the per-model latency histograms and per-instance CPU/GPU utilization for the last 6 hours.
3) Engineering action: Dev, please triage kernel/runloop traces and check for batcher/backpressure regressions; mark any recent runtime rollouts.
4) Interim mitigation: we'll prepare a rapid rollback plan + manual scale-up if needed.

Tom — we'll follow up on the call with a concise RCA timeline and proposed credit scope if SLA is at risk.

Kimberly Park

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Tom Alvarez <tom@blueleafanalytics.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 1 Dec 2027 10:27:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Urgent: Growing latency tail, errors & throughput drop — need help

Summary from triage (short):
- Root observation: the runtime batcher introduced an "aggressive-window" heuristic in last night's rollout (2027-12-01 01:13 UTC). For high-concurrency customers this increases batch sizes but also increases head-of-line blocking when downstream NVLink/KV access stalls.
- Failure mode: while overall throughput occasionally improves, the tail spikes dramatically because larger batches amplify any slow instance. With Dedicated pools that have a fixed concurrency cap, the system hits the cap and starts queueing; our internal queue length grows until request TTLs expire => 502/504s and drops.
- Contributing factor: the cluster autoscaler failed to trigger on the initial spike due to a tagging mismatch on the Dedicated pool (autoscale policy expects tag "dedicated-blueleaf" but nodes were provisioned with "dedicated-blue_leaf").

Immediate mitigations (recommended, in order):
1) Rollback the aggressive-window batcher heuristic (execute via runtime canary rollback: rollback job RB-887). This should reduce head-of-line amplification within 5–10 minutes of completion.
2) Temporary manual scale-up: add 3 GPU workers to BlueLeaf's Dedicated pool to increase concurrency headroom while rollback and autoscaler fix are applied.
3) Short-term routing change: mark indexing routes as low-priority for 2 hours to reduce non-critical load.

I'll attach traces and sampled kernel logs to the ticket. If we proceed with manual scaling and rollback now, I estimate customer-facing impact will drop within 15–30 minutes.

Dev Patel
Senior Software Engineer, Inference Runtime
--
Attached: runtime-traces-20271201.txt (traces, 1.8MB)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Alvarez <tom@blueleafanalytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 2 Dec 2027 12:05:00 -0800
Subject: Executive summary and proposed customer remediation (BlueLeaf)

Tom — follow-up after yesterday's triage and mitigation. Action summary: 

- Root cause (preliminary): runtime batching heuristic introduced 2027-12-01 increased batch sizes and amplified head-of-line blocking when a subset of Dedicated workers experienced NVLink/KV stalls. An autoscaler tag mismatch prevented an immediate capacity response.
- Actions taken: Dev rolled back the aggressive-window batching heuristic to the prior canary (RB-885) at 23:47 UTC; we manually added 3 GPU workers to shift concurrency headroom; indexing traffic was deprioritized.
- Immediate customer impact: we saw p99 drop from >12s to ~2.8s within 18 minutes post-rollback; error rate reduced to 0.15% and queue length returned to baseline.

Next steps we propose: 
1) Postmortem & timeline delivered by EOD tomorrow.
2) Short-term credit offer: one week of service credit on your December invoice.
3) Engineering follow-up: patch autoscaler tagging assertion, add a canary smoke test for batcher heuristic changes, and add a per-account concurrency alert to PagerDuty.

Please confirm if the short-term credit is acceptable; Marissa will follow up with the draft credit agreement for review. If you want an exec-level readout, I can schedule an hour with our SVP of Product and Head of Infra.

Kimberly Park
Sr. Director, Customer Success | Redwood Inference

Attachments: sla-impact-summary.pdf (1 page)
